pageCache.pageTitle: Wellington School Somerset Independent Day & Boarding School
pageCache.text:
Home
Give your child the best start in life at our Nursery School which caters for children aged 3 & 4 years old.
Our nurturing Prep School helps children from Reception to Year 6 (4 to 11 years old) to grow in confidence.
Our Senior School welcomes pupils from 11 to 18 and shares its amazing facilities with our Prep School.
Wellington Sixth Form is a unique community.
The boarding community is central to the rich and diverse environment that is Wellington School.
We offer a range of flexible courses for students.
We live by four concrete principles designed to give our young people everything they need to not just inherit the future, but to create it. ‘Embracing complexity’, ‘Sparking connections’, ‘Leading together’ and ‘Acting today’ form the lens through which we’re designing the future of education. It’s one of the many reasons that this is such an exciting time to join us.
You are always so welcome to visit us, and I look forward to meeting you in person, soon.
International Boarding Student
Prep Director of Sport And Co-curricular
Teacher of Geography
Head of Years 3-6 and Prep Maths Co-ordinator
Head of Religious Studies
Deputy Head of Sixth Form and Head of Rugby

pageCache.pageTitle: Welcome To Nursery  (Age 2 - 4 Years)  - Wellington School Somerset
pageCache.text:
Welcome To Nursery (Age 2 - 4 Years)
Our Nursery with Forest School is an integral part of Wellington School and this is where the excitement begins.
Kate Williams is our passionate lead practitioner dedicated to creating a high-quality, inclusive and nurturing earning environment where every child thrives. She has an NVQ Level 3 qualification and is currently on her own learning journey working towards a degree in Early Childhood Studies. She enjoys long dog walks and at the weekends, you will find her at a National Trust property with her family.
We provide the highest standards of early years education for three and four year olds, making the most of our excellent facilities. A rich variety of learning environments such as our woodland site for embracing nature at Forest School and our Sports Complex for providing the space to gain the basics of riding a bike sees our youngest pupils grow into happy , confident, independent individuals with an enduring love for learning. Our team is led by experienced specialist early years' teachers and lead practitioners.
‘Tell me and I forget; Teach me and I may remember; involve me and I learn.’
You can view the the government's latest Early Years Foundation Stage Handbook here.
Learning For Life Enrichment Programme
At Wellington School we are fortunate to have a superb range of facilities and staff. As a result, we are able to offer an exceptional and unique package of educational enrichment opportunities to our nursery children; our ‘Learning for Life’ enrichment programme.
For those families using the Early Years funding, this programme carries a small additional fee as the services offered are above and beyond most other settings. All families choosing Wellington Nursery School are strongly encouraged to take advantage of the educational and development value from these additional services.
Further information on the cost of the ‘Learning for Life’ programme is available in the Nursery Fees and Charges document here.
Guided Play
Want to know more about this important part of Early Years learning?
Learning Skills - Independent learning in the Early Years
One of the key skills for learning that we want to empower our unique children with is independence, both in relation to their actions and their thinking. This is best done through play. We use our skills and knowledge to provide a play-based learning environment, building on and incorporating children’s interests. We plan and prepare an environment that teaches fundamental skills but provides opportunities for children to put those skills into practice on their own, too. Examples maybe to fill a glue pot, put on a coat for play time or find the resources necessary to create a model. We encourage children to have confidence in their own abilities, through lots of positive reinforcement for their success and support for failures they have along the way. Otherwise, they will remain over reliant on the support of adults or their more confident peers.
GUIDED PLAY
Through a mix of different approaches to helping children learn in our Early Years.
• through play • by adults modelling • through guided learning • direct teaching
Sometimes the staff in the Early Years join in with the child’s play, sensitively, to support and extend the learning. We call this learning in the ‘moment’ or guided play.
LEARNING SKILLS
Play is serious learning for a young child, it is the vehicle they use to develop the skills they need to become effective learners. That it is why it is called the Foundation Stage.
The skills we aim to nurture are…
• language and communication skills • regulation of emotions • the ability to be independent • to be creative and pursue their own ideas • to be resilient in the face of adversity.
Above all, for the children in our care to be kind, considerate, inclusive members of the community.

Our Vision
Excellence Is Only The Beginning
When choosing a school, we naturally look for assurances. We want to see academic strength, superb pastoral care, co-curricular excellence and strong ties to Universities and industry. We’re proud to say that Wellington has all of that in abundance. But to be perfectly frank, any independent school should be able to say the same. In today’s world with the challenges and opportunities that abound, we believe this excellence should only be the beginning. Indeed, we have wanted to ask: What else? What makes Wellington not just exemplary, but extraordinary?
There are a few answers to that question, but at the top of the pile is our pioneering approach to education itself. We live by four concrete principles designed to give our young people everything they need to not just inherit the future, but to create it. ‘Embracing complexity’, ‘Sparking connections’, ‘Leading together’ and ‘Acting today’ form the lens through which we’re designing the future of education. It’s one of the many reasons that this is such an exciting time to join us.
Something else that makes us extraordinary is our community. No other school I’ve come across has a culture more nurturing, respectful and kind than ours. You’ll feel it the minute you get here. It’s what makes this place a second home; a place and a family, that your child will cherish for the rest of their lives.
We passionately believe that Wellington is uniquely positioned to support your child’s journey. We offer both historical stability and fresh perspectives; excellence in all areas combined with progressive practices, and a community as inspiring as it is welcoming.
Our vision is to lead the future of education as a transformational community where young people help create the future (and aren’t just prepared for it). To deliver that for our students, we will design the practicalities of our offer around the following four principles for the future of education. Click on the links below to find out more:

Act Today
Don’t wait for the future to happen. Life has started. Don't be resigned to inheriting the future. Make a mark on the world here and now and doing so will only build your purpose.

Embrace Complexity
Don’t try to control everything. Stay grounded and curious. Embrace emergence. Become used to working in systems that don’t have simple cause and effect.

Lead Together
Don’t miss out on other people’s ideas and energy. Invite them in, to multiply what’s possible. Work with hierarchies and collaborate and influence outside of them. Learn to inspire communities around shared purpose.

Spark Connections
Don’t limit your perspective. Use an entrepreneurial mindset. Link knowledge, people, concepts and experiences to create something new. The world is inter-connected; our thinking should reflect that.

The School Day
We have buses bringing children in from all around the region which arrive at 8.15am. Assembly, House meetings or tutor groups take place each morning before lessons start at 8.55am.
There are 5 lessons in the School day with three before lunch with a 20 minute break at 11.05am and then two further lessons after lunch. Lunchtimes are 80 minutes, which allows students to engage with the many clubs and societies on offer during this time.
School finishes at 3.45pm when our wide-ranging clubs programme begins and buses leave School at 5.00pm.

Technical Theatre
Over the past few years we have built up a talented technical team of students in school.
Our technical team support the performers with putting on their shows and productions. We are one big team. You can choose to specialise in lighting, sound, costume or set design and your enthusiasm in these areas are fostered and your skills are developed.
We have a Drama Tech Club, which runs each week and these students learn stage management, lighting and sound skills. These students have access to industry professionals, including award-winning Lighting Designer, David Bishop, who has worked on BBC's Strictly Come Dancing, X Factor and Royal Weddings and Celebrations. They also work on all school productions during the year.

pageCache.pageTitle: National Youth Theatre - Wellington School Somerset
pageCache.text:
National Youth Theatre
We are immensely proud of the 20 students from Wellington School who have gained entry into the prestigious National Youth Theatre over the past five years, following in the footsteps of Old Wellingtonian, Sir David Suchet.
Their remarkable achievement reflects their dedication, talent, and hard work, as well as the outstanding support and guidance provided by our staff. This accomplishment not only highlights their individual potential but also underscores our commitment to nurturing young talent and fostering a thriving artistic community. We look forward to witnessing their continued growth and success in the world of theatre.
Students gain entry through school based auditions. The National Youth Theatre opens doors to world-class training and performance opportunities, and we are delighted to see so many of our students rise to this prestigious challenge.
National Youth Theatre
The National Youth Theatre (NYT) was established in 1956 and is a pioneering organisation in youth arts education. It provides young people aged 14-25 with unique opportunities to engage in professional theatre production and training. Admission into the NYT is highly competitive and is regarded as a significant achievement for any young aspiring actor. Once you gain entry you are a member until the age of 25!
Benefits of being part of the National Youth Theatre Company
One of the primary benefits of being part of the NYT is the comprehensive training it provides. Successful applicants undergo rigorous and high-quality training programs that cover various aspects of theatre. These programs are designed to hone acting skills, develop stagecraft, and improve overall performance abilities. Workshops and masterclasses are led by industry professionals, offering invaluable insights and techniques.
Members of the NYT also get the chance to participate in full-scale theatrical productions, often staged at renowned venues such as the National Theatre, the Royal Court, and the Edinburgh Fringe. These productions are not just amateur performances but are held to professional standards, giving young actors real-world experience in the theatre industry. This hands-on experience is crucial for those looking to pursue a career in acting.
Being part of the National Youth Theatre opens doors to an extensive network of industry contacts. Members have the chance to work with established actors, directors, producers, and other theatre professionals. This networking is invaluable for career development, providing young actors with connections that can lead to future opportunities in theatre, film, and television.
The company has a storied history of producing successful alumni who have gone on to make significant contributions to the arts. Notable alumni include actors such as Daniel Craig, Helen Mirren, and our very own OW Sir David Suchet. The success of its alumni serves as an inspiration and testament to the quality of training and opportunities.
The National Youth Theatre offers an unparalleled platform for young people passionate about theatre. Through its comprehensive training programs, professional production opportunities, and extensive support network, the NYT equips its members with the skills, experience, and confidence needed to succeed in the competitive world of performing arts. For young actors, gaining entry into the NYT can be a transformative experience, paving the way for future success both on and off the stage.

Art
Our Aim
The Art and Design curriculum aims to foster creativity through the analysis of art and ideas and equip students with the necessary core skills in art, craft and design, so students can realise their own creative intentions. We aim to produce fully independent art practitioners, with the confidence to discuss ideas and concepts and to use materials in an analytical, expressive and conceptual ways. We develop the students' visual awareness by fostering an environment of observation and purposeful play and subsequent critical reflection, where students can develop their own art practice. We firmly believe everybody is creative, that we can nurture talent and support all students to find their creative voice through a progressive and flexible curriculum. It is our fundamental belief that we offer the students a truly creative education - to teach creativity we need to teach creatively.
How?
The Art curriculum is based around a series of thematic frameworks that allows space for students to explore and investigate the work of others, understand the formal elements of art and art-making through a broad range of media, scale and dimensions. We do not have a house style nor a prescriptive way of making – this is governed by students understanding of artwork and their own personal response to art and wider societal concerns. Students are encouraged to think and make creative statements - to produce visually effective work with confidence. Students are encouraged to take on the role of artists and designers, making use of guided and self-originated strong contextual references to develop their own ideas. We celebrate the big what if, try things out, experiment and see where it leads.
We Give Students The Freedom
• to be resourceful, curious and creative • to engage with the world around them, preferably outside of the classroom • to work in a specific area of study related to own specialisms and strengths • respond to themes critically and with individuality • to be inventive in their experimentation • to engage with many starting points and possibilities • to foster and sustain their exploratory play.
The Art Curriculum
• Years 5 and 6 guided learning: three modules a year with the final module being a thematic exploration • Years 7 and 8: three modules, one guided set theme then two modules students explore thematically • Year 9 taught thematically and open ended as GCSE • Years 10, 11, 12 and 13 are taught thematically leading to the development of the student's own coursework interests and specialisms. Year 13, in addition, time is given to portfolio preparation for those students moving directly onto Art based degree course of study.
